summary: afisha-storybook-default postinstall dropper fetches and executes remote payload with DNS TXT fallback
details: The package's postinstall script (also invoked when the module is required) downloads a platform-specific executable from Cloudflare Workers subdomains whose hostnames are reconstructed at runtime from split-string arrays (e.g. ["oob-wor","ker.cf","99-9b3.wor","kers",".dev"].join("")). If the HTTP fetch fails, a fallback resolves a count from a 'c.<domain>' DNS TXT record then iterates numeric subdomains under *.dl.well1.site, concatenates the TXT record contents, and base64-decodes them to reconstruct the payload bytes — a covert DNS-tunneled delivery channel. The reconstructed bytes are written to /var/tmp (POSIX) or %TEMP% (Windows) under disguised names mimicking legitimate artifacts (dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe,.cache_<hex>), chmodded 0755 on POSIX, and launched detached with unref via execFile. A stamp file at /tmp/.analytics_state and 'telemetry/analytics' identifier framing provide cover. setup.js also invokes execSync('powershell...') on Windows. There is no hash/signature verification of the downloaded bytes, no relationship between the delivery hosts and any legitimate publisher, and the hostname obfuscation is a deliberate evasion of static scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
